title: Rate Book — Electric Service by Rate Schedule Monthly Facility and Energy Rates
content:
The monthly rates of Electric Service by Rate Schedule are set schedule by schedule. Every billing period carries a fixed facility charge and an energy charge priced in two blocks: the kWh of the period up to the block 1 limit are billed at the block 1 rate, and the kWh above the limit at the block 2 rate. Energy rates are stated per kWh to five decimals.

| Term | R | RS | FH | GS-1 | GS-3 | IR | LP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Facility charge per billing period | $32.50 | $38.75 | $36.00 | $42.00 | $68.50 | $54.00 | $245.00 |
| Energy rate, block 1 (per kWh) | $0.11840 | $0.12610 | $0.11840 | $0.11275 | $0.10460 | $0.08915 | $0.06380 |
| Block 1 limit (kWh per billing period) | 1000 | 1000 | 1500 | 2500 | 5000 | 20000 | 200000 |
| Energy rate, block 2 (per kWh above the limit) | $0.10920 | $0.12610 | $0.10420 | $0.10350 | $0.09715 | $0.08915 | $0.05845 |
| Power cost adjustment line billed | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| State sales tax on the period's taxable lines | 0.00% | 6.50% | 0.00% | 6.50% | 6.50% | 0.00% | 6.50% |

Column key: R is Schedule R Residential Service; RS is Schedule RS Seasonal Residential Service; FH is Schedule FH Farm and Home Service; GS-1 is Schedule GS-1 Single-Phase General Service; GS-3 is Schedule GS-3 Three-Phase General Service; IR is Schedule IR Irrigation Service; LP is Schedule LP Large Power Service.

### Notes to the rate sheet

1. On Schedule RS and Schedule IR the block 1 and block 2 rates are the same figure, so every kWh of the period is billed at one rate whatever the usage. On the other five schedules the block 2 rate is lower than the block 1 rate.
2. The monthly wholesale power cost adjustment line is billed on all seven schedules.
3. A sales tax of 0.00% means the schedule is exempt; Schedules R, FH and IR are exempt, and Schedules RS, GS-1, GS-3 and LP carry 6.50%.

### Hypothetical example — pricing a period's kWh on Schedule R

A Schedule R period of 1,250 kWh (hypothetical usage) prices 1,000 kWh at $0.11840, which is $118.40, and the remaining 250 kWh at $0.10920, which is $27.30, for an energy charge of $145.70. A period of 900 kWh stays wholly within block 1 and prices at $0.11840 per kWh, which comes to $106.56.
